name: weak-repro-keyed-ab
description: PRE-REGISTERED 2026-07-30, before any run. keyed-task-pool fails 9/15 on the local 27B, always as an async deadlock ('Promise resolution is still pending'). Not a spec gap (the task states the lifecycle contract), not an inert mechanism (the async state audit fires 14/15 and the model engages 2-14 times). A turn-level counterfactual injecting the hidden grader's exact error moved the model 3/6 re-done to 0/6 and 6/6 to `node --test` -- it reran its ONLY oracle, the public suite, which passes. DIAGNOSIS: oracle gap. The public suite is 6 assertions against the grader's 25 and runs everything at concurrency 1 with a single key, so it cannot observe queue drain, FIFO across keys, capacity release on a synchronous throw, or onIdle with queued work -- exactly the failing hidden tests. HYPOTHESIS: strengthening the public repro FROM THE TASK'S STATED INVARIANTS (not from the grader) raises the hidden pass rate, because the model can finally see its own bug. keyed-task-pool-strong is identical in task text, starting stubs and hidden grader; only the public test file differs, and its four added tests were validated green against a correct pool and red against the stubs. PRIMARY METRIC: hidden-contract pass rate. FALSIFIED IF: the strengthened arm does no better, which would mean the failure survives a working oracle and is a reasoning limit after all.
